league.t: In each of Weeks 1 through 13, the franchise with the lowest score pays $50 into the penalty pool. That money buys bitcoin, which is held separately from the luxury pool. The fine is called out in the Dispatch and on the home page every week.
The penalty pool is paid out after Week 14. Half goes to the team with the most points in the whole league that week. A quarter goes to the team with the second-most.
The last quarter of the pool goes to the team with the highest single-week score from Weeks 1 through 13. The current record holder is shown on the home page, and every new record is announced.

A tied score in any weekly result (a head-to-head game, the weekly low score, the Week 14 Free-For-All or a playoff game) is broken by bench points that week. More bench points wins, except for the low score, where the team with fewer bench points pays.

moves.t: During the season, players are added through free agency or through blind-bid waivers. Which one applies depends on the day and on whether the player’s game has started.
Free agency opens every Thursday at 9 a.m. ET. Until a player’s NFL game kicks off that week, anyone can add or drop him, and the move goes through right away.
At kickoff of his NFL game, a player locks for the rest of the week. From then until waivers run, he can only be added with a blind-bid waiver claim.
Waivers run every Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET. Each claim includes a bid from the team’s budget, and the highest bid wins the player. The site prompts for a bid whenever an add falls inside the lock.
Each team gets $1,000 in blind-bid dollars for the season. FAAB is separate from auction dollars. Once a team’s FAAB runs out, it can only add players through free agency for the rest of the season.
FAAB dollars can be included in trades, but only during the current season. They never carry over to the next year.

playoffs.t: Eight teams make the playoffs. Six spots are set when the regular season ends after Week 13. The last two are decided in Week 14.
The three division winners get in automatically. A division is won by the best overall record in it. If records are tied, the team with more total season points wins the division.
The three teams with the best records among the non-division-winners also get in, using the same total-points tiebreaker. Seeds 1 through 6 are now set.
The teams ranked 7th through 10th after Week 13 play one week against each other at once. Head-to-head results don't count. Only each team's total score matters.
Points are added to Week 14 scores based on rank after Week 13. The 7th-place team gets 100 points and the 8th-place team gets 50. The 9th- and 10th-place teams start from zero.

The two highest Free-For-All scores, head start included, earn the last two playoff spots. Between them, the team ranked higher after Week 13 is listed first. The final seeds aren’t set until the division winners pick their opponents.
Before the first round, the three division winners each choose their opponent from the other playoff teams. The 1 seed picks first, then the 2 seed, then the 3 seed.
The two teams nobody picks play each other in the first round. For the rest of the playoffs, those two are the 4 and 5 seeds.
The four first-round winners move on to the semifinals. The highest remaining seed picks its opponent, and the other two teams play each other.

draft.t: Each year, a rookie draft is held before the auction draft. It is one round, and every team gets one pick. The order is set by the Rookie Lottery.

The Commish draws the rookie draft order on the Rookie Lottery page. Each ball is one chance at the #1 pick. Pick 1 is drawn first, then pick 2 from the teams left, and so on. The official result is posted on the site.
Every team starts with 20 balls. A team that misses the playoffs gets 20 more.
A team loses 5 balls for every playoff game it wins, starting in Week 15. The Week 14 Free-For-All does not count.
A team loses 1 ball for every $1 of next year’s auction money it has gained in trades. Only net gains count, and a team that traded money away does not gain balls. No team can go below zero balls.

Each drafted rookie is given a salary based on the pick used. The first pick is worth $25, and each pick after it is worth $3 less, down to $4 at pick 8. Picks 9 through 12 are also worth $4. Pick 1 is $25, pick 2 is $22, pick 3 is $19, pick 4 is $16, pick 5 is $13, pick 6 is $10, pick 7 is $7, and picks 8 through 12 are $4.

A team that doesn’t want a player at its pick’s value may pass and move to the end of the order. When it picks later, the player gets the value of the pick slot it actually uses. For example, a team that passes at pick 2 picks last and pays $4.
The league holds an auction draft every year. Each team starts with a $200 budget to bid on players.

This is a keeper league. Before each auction, a team may keep any players from its roster at the end of the previous season. Kept players’ salaries count against that year’s auction budget. Plan keepers on any team page with Plan Keepers.

Every kept player’s salary goes up, and the raise depends on how many players a team keeps. Each kept player goes up by one dollar more than the number kept. Keeping 1 player adds $2 to his salary. Keeping 2 adds $3 to each, keeping 3 adds $4 to each, and so on.

Players picked up during the season, through FAAB or free agency, carry a $0 salary for the rest of that season. A kept pickup costs $10 if the team keeps 3 or fewer players. Above that, he costs $1 more for each extra keeper: $11 with 4 keepers, $12 with 5, and so on. Every other kept player’s raise is added to his salary on MFL at the end of the season.
Auction dollars for next year’s draft can be traded. A team’s budget can rise or fall by up to $30 through trades, so every team enters the auction with between $170 and $230.
Right before each auction, a team may pay extra dues to add up to $20 to its auction budget. The budget, including traded dollars, still can’t go over the $230 cap.

Each of the first 10 added dollars costs one-tenth of annual dues ($25 at $250 dues). Each dollar from the 11th through the 20th costs one-fifth of annual dues ($50). Adding $10 costs $250, and adding the full $20 costs $750.
80% of luxury tax collected is invested in bitcoin. The other 20% is invested at Bloodfeast’s discretion. The pool is added to league dues, so the yearly awards rise or fall with its value.

The $170–$230 limit applies only to next year’s auction budget. Once the season starts, a team may go above or below that range during the year. The limit is checked against the budget each team brings to the next auction.
Next year’s auction dollars and rookie picks can be included in any trade proposed on the site. Once the trade is accepted, both teams’ budgets and pick ownership update automatically.

rules.t: Restricted free agency opens the new fantasy year, usually in mid-August, before the rookie draft and the auction. The league has held RFAs every year since 2018; the full history is on the History page.
Every team must put one player from its roster into the RFA pool by RDPC's deadline. If a team doesn't, RDPC picks one for it.
A player who was an RFA the previous season can't be put in the pool. This rule has been in place since 2022.
For 12 days, RDPC draws one player a day from the pool at random.

The other 11 teams each submit a blind bid in whole dollars, starting at $1, plus a number of penalty shots, or pass. The bid is the player's salary for the coming auction. The team whose player is up sits out.
A bid can't be more than the bidding team's next-year auction budget. RFA salaries come out of that budget, and a team can win more than one RFA.

The highest bid wins. If bids are tied, the one with more penalty shots wins. If two bids are tied on dollars and shots, and the original team doesn't match, the tied teams settle it with a three-cup flip-cup relay at the draft. The winner gets the player.

The original team then sees the top bid and can match it, keeping the player at that salary and taking the penalty shots, or let him go to the top bidder, who takes the shots. If nobody bids, the player stays put.
RDPC runs the process. Bids stay sealed, even from the Commish, until each player is resolved. Then every bid and shot count is posted on the RFA page.
The Pro Bowl is played in NFL Week 18, the week after the Dubcey championship in Week 17.
It's a divisional competition. Each of the three divisions fields one lineup from its four teams' rosters.
Each division lineup has 2 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 TE and 2 FLEX (RB, WR or TE), scored the same as a regular week.
The four owners in a division fill the open spots on the Pro Bowl page with players from their own rosters. Owners can swap or pull their own players until that player's game kicks off.
Every team must have at least one player on its division's roster. When the open spots only cover the teams still missing, those spots are saved for them.
Each player locks when his Week 18 game kicks off.
Every team puts in $50. The division with the highest total wins, and its four teams split the $600 pot, $150 each.
Every franchise has one main helmet, set by the Commish. Owners can't replace or delete it.
Any owner can design a new helmet in the Helmet Lab and add it to their team as an alternate. Owners can add alternates but can't remove any. Only the Commish can take one down.

In the Helmet Lab, an owner picks which helmet the site shows each week: the main helmet, one of the alternates, or a weekly rotation through all of them. The Commish can still pin a helmet for a special week.
Every helmet wears the Dubcey patch, in the same spot and at the same size. The Helmet Lab won't make a helmet without it.
